Subject: Post-demo technical alignment: SDK setup & adaptive model policy

Hi Sophie — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick written summary and recommended next steps so we have a shared checklist for the POC.

Recap (what we covered)
- SDK onboarding: server-side + client examples, service account vs long-lived API keys
- Auth: short-lived tokens, optional SAML SSO for web UI flows
- Routing/policy: latency-first for interactive UI; cost-aware for bulk re-ranks; fallback chain options
- Structured output/tool-calling: function-calling patterns for controlled actions (intent -> tool call)
- Embeddings & reranker: managed vector store vs bring-your-own; candidate reranking stage described

Immediate asks from your team (from notes):
1) Sample SDK snippet for server-side token refresh and a node/python example for streaming responses
2) Clarify EU region residency and routing behavior (anything required for PHI)
3) Ballpark cost guidance for a 3-week POC (100k inference tokens/day + 50k embedding ops)
4) POC timeline and required artifacts from Skyline (sample data, acceptance tests)

Proposed technical approach (high level)
- SDK: use our server-side SDK with service account creds. We issue short-lived tokens for browsers.
- Auth: SSO for engineers (SAML) + token-based service accounts for backend.
- Routing & policy: define two policies — "interactive" (latency SLO p95 <200ms) and "batch-rerank" (cost-prioritized). Policy engine routes to model variants by sequence length and current capacity; fallback chain: high-accuracy model -> quantized cheaper variant -> local cache (k-NN)
- Structured output: function-calling hook + strict schema enforcement for actions; recommended sandboxing for side effects.
- Embeddings: we recommend managed hosting for faster MLP index + optional export. Reranker pipeline: retrieval -> coarse model -> reranker model -> final score.

Next steps / action items
- Connor: send SDK snippet + call recording + initial design doc (attached) — by EOD today
- Marissa: schedule 90-min architecture workshop with your eng + devops for Wed 3/17 10am PT (proposed)
- Skyline: confirm POC dataset availability and any compliance constraints (PHI)

Attachments: call-recording-20270312.mp3, draft-mma-connector-design.pdf

Thanks — happy to adjust if we missed anything.

Hi Sophie — quick technical responses inline to help unblock the eng review.

1) Token rotation / SDK
- We recommend service accounts + short-lived JWTs minted by our control plane. Sample Node snippet attached (sdk-snippet.js). Pattern: backend mints short-lived token (TTL 5m) -> UI exchanges via secure cookie. For server-to-server flows you can use our long-lived service account key stored in your KMS and rotate monthly.
- Streaming: our SDK supports HTTP/2 streaming and chunked websocket clients. The Node snippet shows a stream handler that emits partial tokens to the UI.

2) Region/residency and routing pinning
- You can pin a policy to a region (e.g., eu-central-1). When pinned, fallbacks will only use models with the same region tag unless you explicitly allow cross-region failover. For PHI we recommend strict pinning + Dedicated capacity in the EU (Redwood Private) to avoid any cross-region fallback.

3) Embeddings guidance
- 1536-d vectors: better semantic fidelity, ~20-30% higher index size/cost vs 1024-d. For ~10M docs we recommend compressed/quantized indexes + managed vector store; BYO can work but you’ll need sharding and autoscaling. We support AES-256 encryption at rest for managed indexes.
- Latency: 1536-d retrieval p50 ~12-20ms on our managed index for the size you mention; 1024-d typically 8-12ms.

4) Model routing / fallback pattern (concrete suggestion)
- Policy: define two named policies: interactive-ui (SLO p95 <200ms) and rerank-batch (cost-first).
- Routing rules: route by intent + token budget. Example: interactive-ui -> gauss-xxl (if p95 capacity) else gauss-quantized -> cached k-NN; rerank-batch -> gauss-sm -> gauss-quantized.
- Fallback behavior: policy engine emits metrics and will not cross region unless allowed.

5) POC checklist / blockers
- We need: sample data (anonymized), defined acceptance tests (latency thresholds + quality eval prompt set), and a point of contact for DevOps to provision network allowlists.

Attachments: sdk-snippet.js (example token rotation + streaming)

Happy to run the 90-min architecture workshop on Wed 3/17 10am PT (proposed by Connor). If EU Dedicated is required for PHI we should surface procurement early.

— Marissa (Solutions Architect)
